chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), when he stood for prayer, his color would change. And when he prostrated, he would not raise his head until he perspired profusely.
ai.seo_question: What were the physical signs of Ali ibn Al-Husayn's devotion during prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* under the chapter on humility (*Khushu*), this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the ideal state of *Khushu* where spiritual presence overwhelms the physical form. The scholar al-Kulayni uses this to demonstrate that true devotion is not merely ritualistic but manifests in tangible physical signs, such as the change in complexion and prolonged prostration until sweating, reflecting the depth of one's connection with the Divine.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzān, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said:
‘It was that whenever Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws, stood regarding the Salāt, hisasws colour changed. So when heasws performed Sajdah, did not raise hisasws head until heasws perspired profusely’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rib‘i ibn ‘Abd Allah from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would stand up for Salah (prayer), the color of his face change and in sajdah he remained so long until (his face) became drenched with perspiration (and tears).”
